text:
maria-support: Customer on Pro tier reports streaming cutoffs during long-poll SSE calls. They see the stream return a few chunks then abruptly stop and client reconnects. Only happens when going through Cloudflare + our NLB in us-west-2. Direct requests to the ALB (bypass CF) seem stable. Request id: r-7c4f9, sample curl in thread.

sam-eng: ack. can you paste the minimal curl repro and the exact behavior? does the client get a TCP RST or an HTTP close? any 5xx from our side?

maria-support: here's the repro we gave customer:
```
curl -v \\\n  -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \\\n  -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" \\\n  "https://api.redwood-inference.example/v1/stream?model=gptj"
```
They get some events like `data: ...` then after ~40s the connection closes. Browser console shows network disconnected, no 5xx body, sometimes a Cloudflare 524 in their logs.

support-bot: quick dump from their provided response headers (sanitized):
```
CF-Ray: 78a1:abcd
Server: nginx/1.18.0
Connection: close
```
They also attached a pcap showing a FIN after the last chunk.

jonathan-infra: interesting — Cloudflare has a 100s HTTP request timeout but I've seen their edge WAF or workers cut streams earlier if they detect perceived inactivity. NLB behavior: if the TCP connection is idle and there's any half-close behavior or missing keepalives it can drop sooner under load. Can you confirm whether the app is sending any heartbeat comments? SSE heartbeats (a comment line `: \n` every 15s) help keep intermediaries happy.

sam-eng: also check our side logs for `upstream prematurely closed connection` or `client closed connection`. From the runtime traces I see no internal 5xx around r-7c4f9. Could be the proxy between CF and NLB closing. We should try three things:
1) reproduce with `curl --no-buffer` directly to NLB endpoint (bypass CF)
2) reproduce through CF but force a heartbeat every 10s from the app
3) tcpdump on the NLB target to confirm FIN vs RST

maria-support: I ran a quick bypass test with the customer's payload and direct NLB URL — stream stayed alive for 5 minutes. Through Cloudflare it cuts at ~40s. Customer also mentioned that when they refresh auth token and reconnect they sometimes get 401 on the reconnect attempt. Could be separate auth timing.

jonathan-infra: that points at CF interplay. Two likely vectors: (A) Cloudflare Workers/WAF or rate limiting closing long lived requests; (B) CF expecting application-level keepalives and closing on perceived silence. Workaround: add SSE comment heartbeats and ensure chunked flush on server (use `fflush`/`res.flush()` depending on runtime). Also set header `Connection: keep-alive` and `Cache-Control: no-transform` to prevent middleboxes coalescing chunks.

sam-eng: for reproducibility, try this small node snippet to send heartbeat:
```js
res.write(':heartbeat\\n\\n'); // SSE comment line keeps proxies from idling
res.flush && res.flush();
setInterval(() => { res.write(':hb\\n\\n'); res.flush && res.flush(); }, 15000);
```
If adding that fixes it for the customer, it's likely proxy idle gating.

maria-support: customer tried adding a client-side keepalive (XHR ping every 20s) and _that_ kept the stream open consistently. So workaround confirmed. They asked whether we can push a platform change (server-side heartbeat) to avoid them having to change client code.

jonathan-infra: we can enable SSE comments by default for streaming endpoints but need to validate resource impact. Low risk: send a `:heartbeat\\n\\n` every 15s while tokens are valid. Watch for any downstream billing impact (extra bytes). Also investigate Cloudflare rules: ask customer to provide CF Ray ID and request headers so we can open a CF ticket. If CF is returning 524/522 inconsistently that's a CF side issue.

sam-eng: also note the reconnect 401 — our reconnect auth flow should accept fresh tokens. If client tries to reuse an expired token during reconnect, we'll correctly 401. Recommend that client refresh token proactively before reconnect, or we add a retry-on-401 exchange: when stream reconnects immediately exchange temporary credentials without dropping the user session. I'll open a small RFC to standardize reconnection semantics.

maria-support: action items:
- sam: add small server-side SSE heartbeat toggle (feature flag, default on for streaming endpoints) and monitor for regressions (deploy -> prod canary).
- jonathan: open CF support ticket with the customer's CF-Ray + sample logs; confirm if any WAF or worker rules could cause early close.
- sam: add server-side logging to emit `sse-heartbeat-sent` for traces so we can correlate with cutoffs and billing.
- maria: tell customer the temporary workaround (client XHR ping or server heartbeat) and ask for CF-Ray + pcap if they can.

infra-bot: deploy request created: infra/deploys#1234 (sam/heartbeat-sse) canary to dedicated staging group.

maria-support: thanks — I've told the customer we'll try server-side heartbeat and chase CF. Keeping this thread open, will update with CF ticket number and canary results. :thumbsup:
